missing: efficacy: a candidate earlier `same` in 2014. Vallon 2014 (Akita, empagliflozin, glucose 517-535 -> 187-237 mg/dl) and Perkins 2014 (https://doi.org/10.2337/dc13-2338, NCT01392560, same product, 'Mean A1C decreased from 8.0 ± 0.9% ... to 7.6 ± 0.9% (P < 0.0001)') plus Cherney 2014 ('Empagliflozin reduced hemoglobin A1c significantly in both groups, despite lower insulin doses') are both 2014 publications; if a single-arm open-label PoC qualifies as the patient side, efficacy `same` dates to 2014 (model Akita mouse, product_in_model true, model_filed false) rather than 2017. The drafter already quotes Perkins 2014 in the engagement judgement, so the source was in hand.

engagement entry 2 judgement should drop 'whether Cherney cites Vallon's Akita data directly is unverified': the reference list is now checked (Europe PMC, 50 refs) and it does not; it cites Vallon 1999 JASN, Thomson 2011 AJP Regul (STZ rat, SGLT2 blockade), Malatiali 2008 (phlorizin, diabetic rats), Thorup 2000 (STZ rat TGF) and List & Whaley 2011 ('in animals and humans').
rule_questions: Devenny 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1038/oby.2012.59, abstract verified: 'Fasting BHBA was elevated in the 1 mpk, 5 mpk, and 5 mpk PF-V groups'; also non-fasting BHBA up and RER down in pair-fed rats) is a rodent ketone signal published five years before the clinical DKA signal. I scored it as NOT changing the safety status because (a) it is a different model (DIO rat, obesity context, insulin present) from the insulin-deficient models the class relied on for T1D and from the filed tox package (FDA PharmR: zero ketone mentions); (b) it is ketosis/fuel shift, not ketoacidosis, and the authors frame it as energy-balance physiology, not a safety prediction; (c) rule 1 requires a primary source making the model-vs-patient comparison, and none exists: Perry 2019 does not cite Devenny (it cites Yokono 2014 for fat oxidation). The brief does not say whether an unread signal in a model the class did not rely on can convert `contra`-on-silence into `same`/`neg`; it should state that explicitly. If the rules are revised so that any published rodent signal counts regardless of model or framing, this entry becomes `same` (2012-2017) with a model string of 'DIO rat (Devenny 2012)'.

Engagement `same` 2014: the brief says model = the one the class relied on. Cherney 2014's own references show it relied on STZ-rat tubular-hypothesis work (phlorizin and SGLT2 blockade), not the Akita mouse; Vallon 2014 (Akita, empagliflozin) appeared one month earlier but is uncited. I proposed STZ rat (comparison_stated true, product_in_model false since the rat work used phlorizin/dapagliflozin, model_first_use_year 1999 for the phlorizin proxy or 2011 for selective SGLT2 blockade). Alternative reading: keep Akita because it is the only rodent study with the actual product. The brief should say whether a same-product academic model published alongside the trial outranks the class-proxy model the trial actually cites.

Efficacy `same` 2017: Garg 2017 does not mention the NOD mouse (comparison_stated false). The EMA assessment report contains both the NOD result (section 2.3.1) and the clinical HbA1c result but never juxtaposes them. Under a strict reading of rule 1 this is `untested`; under the cf-cftr precedent (Ramsey 2011 alone supports `same`) it is `same`. I followed the precedent. The brief should state whether a regulatory review that holds both results in one document counts as 'making the comparison'.

Whether a class proxy (phlorizin, Vallon 1999, nonselective SGLT inhibitor) opens the engagement strip for the hyperfiltration question (model_first_use_year 1999) or only the first SGLT2-selective use (dapagliflozin in STZ rats, 2008).
